pr_129692_comments.author: saiteja-madha
pr_129692_comments.body:
Updated the catalog pin from `v0.1.0` to `v0.1.1` (`ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92`).

The new release fixes a Responses API compatibility issue: the original middleware sanitized every string under `input`, which could replace protocol item IDs with bracketed PII aliases and trigger HTTP 400 malformed-ID errors. `v0.1.1` preserves IDs and other protocol metadata while sanitizing model-visible text and tool argument/output payloads.

Source fix PR: https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/pull/2
Release: https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/releases/tag/v0.1.1

Local validation: 16 tests passed, Plugin Doctor passed, checksum manifest passed, and the catalog entry validator passed.

pr_129692_comments.author: teknium1
pr_129692_comments.body: Opened saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway#3 with a fix for fail-open registration when Presidio is missing (middleware now always registers and blocks), runtime spaCy model download (now refused with a clear error), and the missing `provides_middleware` in plugin.yaml. It is stacked on the author's #2 (the currently pinned ead6800). After it merges, update `sha:` in this PR to the merge commit and we'll re-review the delta.

pr_129692_reviews.author: teknium1
pr_129692_reviews.body:
Reviewed at saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway@ead68009
The design is careful: errors inside the callbacks fail closed, tool-argument rehydration is allowlist-only and empty by default, and the vault key handling (HKDF subkeys plus a key-check HMAC) looks sound.

**Needs changes before listing**

1. **Medium:** If `presidio_analyzer` is not installed, `register()` raises while importing `.privacy` (which imports presidio at module top). No middleware gets registered, and Hermes then sends the plaintext request as normal, so a missing dependency silently leaks PII instead of blocking. See [`__init__.py:66-77`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/__init__.py#L66-L77) and [`privacy.py:9-10`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/privacy.py#L9-L10). Fix: make `register()` independent of presidio. Move `BLOCKED_TOOL_RESULT`, `blocked_content_for_key` and `contains_non_text_model_content` into a dependency-free module (or define them in `__init__.py`), so a missing presidio surfaces through `_get_engine` ([`__init__.py:28-35`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/__init__.py#L28-L35)) and blocks requests.
2. **Medium:** When the spaCy model named in [`nlp.yaml:4`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/nlp.yaml#L4) (`en_core_web_lg`) is not installed, Presidio's spaCy engine falls back to `spacy.cli.download`. The first LLM request after enabling the plugin can therefore pip-install a ~560 MB wheel from GitHub, with no hash pinning, into the Hermes runtime. See [`privacy.py:188-189`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/privacy.py#L188-L189). Fix: before `NlpEngineProvider(...).create_engine()`, check `spacy.util.is_package(<model from nlp.yaml>)` and raise a clear error that points to the manual install steps in [`docs/INSTALL.md:50-81`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/docs/INSTALL.md#L50-L81).
3. The manifest doesn't declare the middleware the plugin registers: `plugin.yaml` lists only the two hooks, while `register()` calls `register_middleware` for `llm_request` and `tool_request`. Validation's declared-middleware check will fail once the dependencies are installed. See [`plugin.yaml:12-14`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/plugin.yaml#L12-L14) and [`__init__.py:176-177`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/__init__.py#L176-L177). Fix: add `provides_middleware: [llm_request, tool_request]` to `plugin.yaml`.
4. There is no `requires_hermes` floor, but the vault uses `plugins.plugin_storage.plugin_db`, which first shipped in Hermes 0.20.4. On older Hermes the vault import fails and every request is blocked. See [`vault.py:66-70`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/vault.py#L66-L70). Fix: add `requires_hermes: ">=0.20.4"` to `plugin.yaml` (and the catalog entry).

**Smaller notes (non-blocking)**

- The `[langextract]` extra in [`pyproject.toml:7`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/pyproject.toml#L7) always pulls `langextract`, `openai` and `azure-identity`, even with LangExtract off. Consider making it an optional extra, or document it.
- The vault database is created with the process umask (no chmod), and the alias/kind/lookup columns are stored in plaintext. Consider `0600` on the file.
- Tools outside `rehydrate_tool_allowlist` receive alias tokens, so for example a `write_file`/`patch` after an aliased `read_file` writes `[PERSON_...]` into the user's files. This is only partly documented ([`docs/GMAIL.md:68-70`](https://github.com/saiteja-madha/hermes-privacy-gateway/blob/ead68009b0bb0f27a0b0f397d32181d35333fb92/docs/GMAIL.md#L68-L70)); a short README note would help.

Push a new commit, update `sha:` in this PR, and we'll re-review the delta.
